issues.legal_issue: A widow’s authority to adopt ends when a grandson or the son’s widow competent to continue the family line by adoption intervenes, and does not revive if that successor later dies.
material_facts: A widow’s husband died leaving a son and two widows, one of whom had authority to adopt.
The son later died leaving a widow and a son, either of whom could continue the family line; the son’s widow died and the grandson died soon afterwards.
Many years after the grandson’s death, the surviving widow adopted the appellant.
The courts below upheld the fact of adoption but held that the widow’s authority to adopt had ended when the son died leaving a widow and a son. The appeal challenged the validity of the adoption.
issues.conclusion: The widow’s authority to adopt had ended when a competent successor to continue the line intervened and did not revive after that successor later died. The adoption was therefore invalid, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the rule established in Hindu law, a widow’s power to adopt ends when a grandson or the son’s widow competent to continue the line by adoption intervenes; the power does not revive when that successor later dies. The rule is not based on vesting or divesting of property, nor is it displaced merely because the son attained ceremonial competence. The Court applied the principles in Bhoobun Moyee v. Ram Kishore, Padma Coomari v. Court of Wards, Thayammal and Kuttisami Aiyan v. Venkatarama Aiyan, Tarachurn v. Suresh Chunder, Ramkrishna Ramchandra v. Shamrao, Madana Mohana v. Purushothama Deo, Amarendra Mansing v. Sanatan and Vijaysingji v. Shivsangji. It rejected the contrary reasoning in Bapuji v. Gangaram and Prem Jagat Kuer v. Harihar Bakhsh Singh, and noted that Shrinivas Krishnarao Kango v. Narayan Devji Kango had declined to accept one proposition in Anant Bhikappa Patil v. Shankar Ramchandra Patil.

rule.if: widow_adoption_validity_appeal and widow_had_adoption_authority and competent_successor_interposed and competent_successor_later_died

predicates.widow_adoption_validity_appeal: An appeal challenged the validity of an adoption made by a widow.
predicates.widow_had_adoption_authority: The widow had authority to adopt under her husband’s grant or the applicable Hindu law.
predicates.competent_successor_interposed: A grandson or the son’s widow capable of continuing the family line by adoption intervened after the son.
predicates.competent_successor_later_died: The successor who intervened later died.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a widow’s adoption, she had authority to adopt, a competent successor intervened, and that successor later died, the widow’s adoption power does not revive.
